prompt:
In a physics laboratory, an air track is used to investigate two different types of collision between two gliders, P and Q. Friction between the gliders and the horizontal track is negligible.
Glider P has mass m_P = 0.250 kg and travels to the right with an initial velocity of +1.60 m s^-1.
Glider Q has mass m_Q = 0.750 kg and is initially stationary on the track.

(a) In Experiment 1, the colliding surfaces are fitted with light, springy steel bumpers so that the collision is perfectly elastic.
Calculate:
  (i) the velocity of glider Q immediately after the collision; [2]
  (ii) the velocity of glider P immediately after the collision. [1]

(b) In Experiment 2, the steel bumpers are removed and replaced with small pads of modelling clay. Glider P is again released with an initial velocity of +1.60 m s^-1 towards the stationary glider Q. Upon impact, the gliders stick together and move forward as a combined body.
Calculate:
  (i) the common velocity of the combined gliders after the collision; [1]
  (ii) the total kinetic energy of the combined gliders after the collision; [1]
  (iii) the percentage of the initial kinetic energy that is dissipated into other energy forms during the collision. [1]

response_structure.description: Velocity of glider Q after elastic collision
Velocity of glider P after elastic collision
Total final kinetic energy after coalescing
Percentage of initial kinetic energy dissipated

hints: Set up conservation of momentum: m_P u_P + 0 = m_P v_P + m_Q v_Q.
Set up relative speed condition: u_P - 0 = v_Q - v_P.
Substitute v_P = v_Q - 1.60 into the momentum equation.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Total initial momentum = (0.250 kg)(+1.60 m s^-1) = 0.400 kg m s^-1.
Step 2: Momentum equation: 0.250 v_P + 0.750 v_Q = 0.400 => v_P + 3 v_Q = 1.60.
Step 3: Relative speed equation: 1.60 - 0 = v_Q - v_P => v_P = v_Q - 1.60.
Step 5: Calculate v_P: v_P = 0.800 - 1.60 = -0.800 m s^-1.
common_pitfalls: Writing the relative speed condition with reversed signs: v_P - v_Q = u_P.
Forgetting the negative sign on v_P representing rebound.

hints: When gliders stick together, use (m_P + m_Q) V = m_P u_P.
common_pitfalls: Using relative speed condition on a coalescing collision where it does not apply.

hints: Use the total combined mass 1.000 kg and V = 0.400 m s^-1.
common_pitfalls: Forgetting to square the velocity V.

hints: Calculate initial kinetic energy E_Ki = 0.5 m_P u_P^2.
Loss in kinetic energy = E_Ki - E_Kf.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 2: Energy dissipated = 0.320 J - 0.0800 J = 0.240 J.
common_pitfalls: Calculating percentage remaining (25%) instead of percentage lost (75%).
Dividing by final kinetic energy instead of initial kinetic energy.

hints: Divide the problem into two distinct physical models: elastic in (a) and completely inelastic in (b).
In (a), solve the linear momentum and relative speed equations simultaneously.
In (b), the gliders coalesce into a single mass of 1.000 kg.
solution:
(a)(i) Total initial momentum: p_i = (0.250)(1.60) = 0.400 kg m s^-1.
Momentum equation: 0.250 v_P + 0.750 v_Q = 0.400 => v_P + 3 v_Q = 1.60.
Relative speed equation: 1.60 - 0 = v_Q - v_P => v_P = v_Q - 1.60.
Substitute v_P into momentum equation: (v_Q - 1.60) + 3 v_Q = 1.60 => 4 v_Q = 3.20 => v_Q = +0.800 m s^-1 (to the right).
(a)(ii) v_P = 0.800 - 1.60 = -0.800 m s^-1 (to the left).

(b)(i) By conservation of momentum for coalescing bodies:
(0.250 + 0.750) V = (0.250)(1.60)
1.000 V = 0.400 => V = +0.400 m s^-1 (to the right).
(b)(ii) E_Kf = 0.5 * (1.000) * (0.400)^2 = 0.0800 J.
(b)(iii) E_Ki = 0.5 * (0.250) * (1.60)^2 = 0.320 J.
Energy dissipated = 0.320 - 0.0800 = 0.240 J.
Percentage lost = (0.240 / 0.320) * 100% = 75.0%.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: In Experiment 1, set up 0.250 v_P + 0.750 v_Q = 0.400 and v_Q - v_P = 1.60.
Step 2: Solve to find v_Q = +0.800 m s^-1 and v_P = -0.800 m s^-1.
Step 3: In Experiment 2, total mass is 1.000 kg; 1.000 V = 0.400 => V = +0.400 m s^-1.
Step 4: Compute final kinetic energy: 0.5 x 1.000 x (0.400)^2 = 0.0800 J.
Step 5: Compute initial kinetic energy: 0.5 x 0.250 x (1.60)^2 = 0.320 J.

mark_scheme.criterion: Sets up momentum equation (0.250 v_P + 0.750 v_Q = 0.400) AND relative speed equation (v_Q - v_P = 1.60)
Calculates velocity of glider Q: v_Q = +0.800 m s^-1 (or 0.80 m s^-1 to the right)
Calculates velocity of glider P: v_P = -0.800 m s^-1 (or 0.80 m s^-1 to the left / rebounds)
Calculates common velocity V = +0.400 m s^-1 (or 0.40 m s^-1 to the right)
Calculates final kinetic energy E_Kf = 0.0800 J (or 0.080 J)
